stimulus.title: Height of a point on a waterwheel
stimulus.html: A waterwheel has a radius of 3 meters. Its center is 1 meter above the surface of the water, so the lowest part of the wheel is under water. The wheel turns at a constant speed and completes one full turn every 12 seconds. A point PP on the rim of the wheel is at the top of the wheel at time t=0t = 0 seconds. The sinusoidal function hh models the height of PP above the surface of the water, in meters, at time tt; a negative height means PP is under water. The graph of hh for one full turn is shown with its axes unscaled. The points FF, GG, JJ, KK and MM are on the graph: FF and MM are highest points, JJ is a lowest point, and GG and KK are at the height of the center of the wheel.

parts.label: A
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the points FF, GG, JJ, KK and MM.

rubric.point: The extremes: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F = (0, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J = (6, -2)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = (12, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: a negative height for <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math>, under water

rubric.point: The midline points: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G = (3, 1)</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K = (9, 1)</annotation></semantics></math>

parts.sample: The highest point is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 + 3 = 4</annotation></semantics></math> m and the lowest is <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1 - 3 = -2</annotation></semantics></math> m, 2 m under water. A quarter turn takes 3 seconds. <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F = (0, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G = (3, 1)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J = (6, -2)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>9</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K = (9, 1)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>12</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>4</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M = (12, 4)</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: B
parts.prompt: The function hh is given by h(t)h(t)=asin⁡(b(t+c))+d= a\sin(b(t + c)) + d, where aa, bb, cc and dd are constants. Find values of aa, bb, cc and dd.

accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = -\frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math> with a matching <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math>

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> that fit the graph: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 3</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 3</annotation></semantics></math>, or <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = -3</annotation></semantics></math> with <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = -3</annotation></semantics></math>
accept: any <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c</annotation></semantics></math> that differs from these by a multiple of 12

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d = 1</annotation></semantics></math> (the center), amplitude 3 (the radius), period 12 so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>b</mi><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mn>2</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow><mn>12</mn></mfrac><mo>=</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">b = \frac{2\pi}{12} = \frac{\pi}{6}</annotation></semantics></math>. With <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>a</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">a = 3</annotation></semantics></math> the sine pattern starts (midline, rising) at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 9</annotation></semantics></math>, or one period earlier at <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = -3</annotation></semantics></math>, so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>c</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">c = 3</annotation></semantics></math>: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(t)</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">(</mo><mrow><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>6</mn></mfrac><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo fence="true" stretchy="true">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= 3\sin\left(\frac{\pi}{6}(t + 3)\right) + 1</annotation></semantics></math>. Check: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn><mi>sin</mi><mo lspace="0" rspace="0.1667em">⁡</mo><mfrac><mi>π</mi><mn>2</mn></mfrac><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h(0) = 3\sin\frac{\pi}{2} + 1 = 4</annotation></semantics></math>.

parts.label: C(i)
parts.prompt: Find the average rate of change of hh on the interval [3,6][3, 6], and explain what its sign means in the context of the problem.

rubric.point: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-1</annotation></semantics></math> meter per second, with its meaning: on average <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> moves down 1 meter each second between <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 3</annotation></semantics></math> and <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t = 6</annotation></semantics></math> (the sign is negative because <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> goes from the center's height down to the bottom of the wheel)
accept: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{h(6) - h(3)}{6 - 3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{-2 - 1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -1</annotation></semantics></math> with a correct reason for the negative sign

parts.sample: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mfrac><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo><mo>−</mo><mi>h</mi><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>3</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mrow><mn>6</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\frac{h(6) - h(3)}{6 - 3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mfrac><mrow><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>2</mn><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mn>3</mn></mfrac></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= \frac{-2 - 1}{3}</annotation></semantics></math><wbr><math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo form="infix">=</mo><mo form="prefix" lspace="0" rspace="0">−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">= -1</annotation></semantics></math> meter per second, the slope of the secant line from <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G</annotation></semantics></math> to <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math>. It is negative because <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> moves down, from the height of the center to 2 meters under water.

parts.label: C(ii)
parts.prompt: Is the rate of change of hh increasing or decreasing on the interval (6,9)(6, 9)? Explain your reasoning.

rubric.point: Increasing, with a reason: on <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(6, 9)</annotation></semantics></math> the graph is below its midline and concave up (between the lowest point <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>J</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">J</annotation></semantics></math> and the midline point <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K</annotation></semantics></math>), so <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> rises faster and faster
accept: the rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing because the graph is concave up

<math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing and the rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing

parts.sample: On <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>6</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>9</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(6, 9)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> rises from the bottom of the wheel toward the height of the center. The graph of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is concave up there, so the rate of change of <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h</annotation></semantics></math> is increasing: <math class="pcalc-m"><semantics><mrow><mi>P</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P</annotation></semantics></math> starts rising slowly from the bottom and goes up faster and faster.
